newsitem.title: LATVIA: BALTICS-WORLD BANK WARNS OF OVERCAPACITY IN TRANSIT.
newsitem.headline: BALTICS-WORLD BANK WARNS OF OVERCAPACITY IN TRANSIT.

text.p: The World Bank on Wednesday said that it sees port overcapacity in the Baltics and downward pressure on transit charges despite an expected increase in Russian trade and urged authorities to focus on rehabilitation rather than heavy investment.

"Huge investment would be vulnerable as there is a significant overcapacity in the system and the competitive poressure is big," Lars Jeurling, the World Bank Baltic mission head, told a transit conference.
Russian trade is expected to increase significantly by 2005, the World Bank forecasts.
"For metals, fertilisers and oil products exports will decline and crude oil, timber and grain exports will grow," Jeurling said.
The Balts will have to keep their costs down and improve efficiency by emphasizing better policies, regulations and administratrion procedures.
"Decisions (in Russia) on where to transit cargoes will be made by a large number of of independent enterprises," Jeurling said.
"(They will be motivated by) cost, efficiency and reliability rather than political considerations," Jeurling said.
